steps.label: ¹⁰B absorbs neutrons
lines: The ¹⁰B isotope absorbs neutrons very
strongly. A neutron that reaches a ¹⁰B
nucleus is captured instead of passing
steps.why: The whole answer rests on one property of the isotope, so it has to be stated before the use, and it is the isotope ¹⁰B, not boron in general, that carries it.
common_mistakes: Saying boron absorbs radiation in general. The property named here is neutron absorption by the ¹⁰B isotope.
Writing ¹¹B. It is ¹⁰B that has the high neutron-absorbing power.
steps.memory_tip: It is the lighter isotope that absorbs the neutrons: ¹⁰B, not ¹¹B.
steps.margin_note: The capture reaction ¹⁰B + ¹n → ⁷Li + ⁴He may be added if there is room.

steps.why: The question asks why the borides are used, so the answer has to end on the use — a shield works because the neutrons are absorbed inside it rather than reaching what is behind it.
common_mistakes: Stopping at the property and never naming the use. The question asks why the borides are used, so the answer has to end on the use.
Saying the boride reflects the neutrons. It absorbs them.
steps.memory_tip: Absorb the neutrons and nothing gets through: that is the shield.
steps.margin_note: Naming control rods alongside shields shows the same property at work.

insider_note: Two sentences answer this: ¹⁰B absorbs neutrons, so a boride made with it shields whatever is behind it.
